name: Sonu Infratech Ltd
tagline: Tiny NSE-SME civil/structural EPC contractor built around Reliance Jamnagar work - fast-growing and very cheap, but single-customer-concentrated and just missed its own FY26 topline guidance
business_overview: Sonu Infratech (NSE SME: SONUINFRA, listed May 2022) is a civil and structural engineering contractor: civil works for production plants, heavy structures and culverts, industrial painting, scaffolding and plant maintenance - overwhelmingly at Reliance Industries' Jamnagar complex. It went public in 2022 and acquired Arpit Techno Infra Pvt Ltd in March 2025.
fundamentals_table: Standalone revenue ~Rs 170 Cr; PAT ~Rs 11.4 Cr (results approved 15-May-2026)
H1FY26 revenue +59% YoY (~Rs 71.9 Cr), EBITDA +71% (~Rs 13.5 Cr), PAT +68% (~Rs 5.5 Cr); EBITDA margin ~18.7% (+131 bps)
Management guided ~Rs 210 Cr FY26 revenue; delivered ~Rs 170 Cr - a MISS
fundamentals_narrative: The growth and margin trajectory is genuinely strong - H1FY26 revenue up ~59% YoY with margins expanding - and the stock is optically very cheap at ~6x earnings on a ~Rs 66 Cr market cap. That combination (small base + inflection + low multiple) is what the screen's small-cap rule is built to catch. But the quality caveats are large: revenue is concentrated on a single end-customer (Reliance Jamnagar), the business is working-capital-heavy and order-to-order lumpy, SME-segment liquidity is thin, and - directly against the reason this name was surfaced - the company MISSED its own FY26 topline guidance (Rs 170 Cr actual vs ~Rs 210 Cr guided) even though it had beaten FY25 guidance. The Arpit Techno acquisition (Mar-2025) adds some capability/scale but also integration risk.

verdict_headline: Cheap, fast-growing micro-cap with a real inflection - but a single-customer EPC contractor that just missed its own guidance, so any 10x path is speculative and unconfirmed
verdict_reasoning: External-lead (tier 4.5) from an untrusted X source (@Aditya_joshi12 teaching quiz, 2025-12-14) citing an FY25 guidance beat - a factual datapoint, not a recommendation, and no floor applies

Per the trailing-average-vs-live-inflection rule, a micro-cap with a weak long history but a strong specific recent run (H1FY26 revenue +59%, PAT +68%), a cheap multiple and a small base is scored 10x-in-2-3-years at LOW conviction with an explicit 'unconfirmed' caveat rather than 'neither'

Caveats that keep conviction LOW: single-customer (Reliance) concentration, an FY26 guidance MISS, SME liquidity/disclosure limits, and zero community or trusted validation. Watch: FY27 order inflows, customer diversification beyond Reliance, and whether it re-establishes a credible guidance track record
